incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: Runtime pool 'runtime-pool-eu-1' reporting elevated GPU page faults and OOM kills. Alerts started ~2026-03-14T21:12Z. Error spike correlates with increased tail latency and 503s. Oncall: @Maya.

Maya: I'm on it. First priority: collect nvidia-smi, dmesg, runtime logs and KV cache metrics. Also need customer impact list. I'll coordinate handoff in this thread.

Sam: grabbing logs now. posting samples below.
```
$ nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv
pid, process_name, used_memory
4321, runtime-worker, 23848 MiB
4334, runtime-worker, 23792 MiB
4340, runtime-worker, 23644 MiB
```
Kernel OOMs: found 3 `oom_killer` events on host gpu-08-eu-1 around 21:14Z. dmesg snippet: `Out of memory: Killed process 4340 (runtime-worker) total-vm:12G, anon-rss:22G`

Priya: metric pulls show KV cache entries exploded on evening traffic surge. Prom query: `sum(kv_cache_entries{pool="runtime-pool-eu-1"}) by (instance)` returned 1.1M @20:00 -> 3.6M @21:00. Concurrent avg_seq_len per request jumped from 128 -> 640 (likely longer context).

Priya: also saw `kvcache_growth_rate` spike on worker groups handling chatty-app customers. Potential cause: clients sending long multi-turn sessions without proper prefix pruning.

Diego: quick mitigation suggestions:
- reduce `max_batch_tokens` on the worker group from 2048 -> 1024 (lower memory pressure per batch)
- enable `aggressive_kv_eviction=true` (evict older prefixes earlier)
- throttle new session creation for non-enterprise customers (rate-limit at edge)

Diego: commands to push config (admin API):
```
POST /admin/runtime/config/group/runtime-pool-eu-1
{ \"max_batch_tokens\": 1024, \"aggressive_kv_eviction\": true }
```

Maya: do it. Start with config change (Diego), then route 10% traffic to fallback-medium model (lower memory footprint) while we verify stability. Sam/Leanne, please prepare rolling restart on the three affected hosts once configs are applied.

Sam: applying config now. Patch submitted and accepted by ops-bot.

ops-bot: Config change applied to runtime-pool-eu-1 (config-id: cfg-20260314-01).

Sam: rolling restart in progress: hosts gpu-06/gpu-07/gpu-08. Restart sequence: drain -> restart worker -> smoke test -> bring back.

Leanne: customer impact assessment: support data shows increased 503s for:
- acme-payments (3% of calls, time window 21:12-21:40 UTC)
- chatty-app (12% of calls, multiple customers experiencing latency spikes)
- beta-analytics (5% of calls, some sessions timed out)
I've notified the on-call support lead and posted incident updates to customers in the support queue. Setting severity P2 for now until we confirm full mitigation.

Diego: also observed high host-level GPU fragmentation metrics: `gpu_free_slices` down from 48 -> 6 on affected nodes. Suggest we also run a defrag job if config + restart don't relieve pressure.

Priya: after config change we see immediate drop in kv cache growth rate: sample prom snapshot:
```
kv_cache_entries total: 3.6M -> 1.9M over 10m post change
avg_seq_len: 640 -> 320
```
Latency tail improved ~20% in first 5 minutes per dashboard.

Maya: good. Continue monitoring for 30m. Next actions:
- Sam: finish restarts and confirm no further OOMs
- Diego: prep defrag plan if OOMs return
- Priya: gather timeline + metrics for RCA (put graphs into shared drive)
- Leanne: continue customer comms and incident updates

Sam: restarts complete, smoke tests passed. No new kernel OOM events in last 12m. Traffic routing at 10% fallback remains.

ops-bot: Routing rule updated: 10% traffic -> model-fallback-medium (rule id rt-20260314-ff).

Priya: posting quick timeline (short):
- 21:12 UTC: first page-fault surge and increased tail latency (alerts)
- 21:14 UTC: kernel OOMs start on gpu-08
- 21:20 UTC: config change (max_batch_tokens -> 1024, aggressive_kv_eviction=true)
- 21:22 UTC: routing 10% traffic to fallback-medium
- 21:28 UTC: rolling restarts complete
- 21:33 UTC: OOMs stop; kv cache growth slows; latency stabilizes

Maya: preliminary hypothesis list (in-thread tracking):
1) KV cache growth due to longer-than-usual sequences from a few high-traffic customers (evidence: avg_seq_len jump, kvcache_growth_rate). Next: correlate session IDs and customer ids -> Priya.
2) GPU fragmentation + large batch tokens caused spikes in memory allocation failures (evidence: low `gpu_free_slices`, kernel OOM logs, large per-batch allocations). Next: Diego run defrag analysis and check allocator metrics.
3) Worker memory leak in a specific runtime version leading to steady per-process RSS increase (evidence: sample pmap shows rising RSS over 24h for pid 4321). Next: Sam to check restarts history and app logs for memory spikes.

Please add more hypotheses as you find them and mark status: (open / investigating / ruled out).

Diego: added another: 4) sudden traffic pattern change (bot / test flood) causing many long-context sessions concurrently. Evidence: proxy logs show a handful of client IPs with high connection counts. Investigating whether these are legit customers.

Leanne: support will follow up with affected customers and request session IDs for deeper correlation. I'm tagging this P2 -> will update status to P1 if errors persist.

Maya: current status: mitigations applied and showing positive signals. We'll keep monitoring for 60m. If stable, prepare post-incident RCA doc with timeline, root cause hypothesis, and remediation plan (config guardrails: max_batch_tokens per pool, KV eviction defaults, alert thresholds on kvcache_growth_rate).

Sam: quick logs attached to the shared drive: drive link: https://redwood.internal/drive/incident-1769154321/logs (internal)

Priya: I'll collect dashboards and add annotations.

Maya: handing off to tomorrow's oncall @Ethan for follow-up and RCA write-up. Ethan, please pick this up at 08:00 UTC shift change.

Ethan: ack, I'll take ownership and drive RCA doc + postmortem.

Maya: thanks team. :thumbsup: We'll keep the channel open until Ethan posts the RCA.
